correctness.rationale: For probability Haar and unrestricted complex coefficients, the fourth moment is the ordered pair-sum convolution energy. On the center-free shell the sole repeated unordered sum is zero (three opposite pairs), so the positive-coefficient expansion is 2B_0²−sum |c_λ|⁴+8 sum_{i<j} p_i p_j. Cauchy and opposite-pair AM–GM give 5B_0²/2, with equality in the magnitude bound requiring equal shell moduli when B_0>0. The six cubic corners omit an antipodal pair. For fixed middle vector the displayed 2×2 matrix has squared singular values with sum 3s+4h and product (s+h)², where s is its squared vector norm and h is the product of its two entries. The largest eigenvalue is increasing for 0≤h≤s/2 and at most 9s/2; applying AM–GM to the three pair masses gives the sharp cubic bound sqrt(2/3) B_0^(3/2). This and |int R²|≤B_0 give the stated rational envelope, attained simultaneously for equal aligned shell coefficients. Differentiation has the recorded cubic numerator factor with one positive root; the boundary ratios 5/2 and 1 are lower. At the maximum, equality in the center-quadratic term makes opposite coefficients conjugate after stripping the common phase; the cubic term is then 12b³ cos(arg c_A−arg c_B−arg c_C), forcing the remaining character relation. All those phases attain equality. Pair-sums lie in [-2,2]², so reduction at q≥5 preserves the entire coefficient formula and allows continuous angles. Zero coefficients and the zero polynomial create no further cases.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration corroborates only the local combinatorics; the tensor estimate, optimizer and full equality proof are analytical. No extension below q=5 is reviewed.

value.rationale: The first full centered A2 frequency neighborhood is a natural complete support, not an arbitrary seven-point selection. The exact L²-to-L⁴ synthesis norm and optimal coefficient profile distinguish center loading from the equal-modulus and center-free models. The sharp cubic resonance also eliminates otherwise independent opposite-pair phases, a concrete structural difference with the shell-only classification. This is useful for exact estimates on this lattice stencil and nonaliasing periodic realizations without requiring any broader application.
